title: Surface workbench examples
summary: Fill a loop of four curves with a surface, make a surface through four sections, and join two curves with a blend curve.

credit.source: Surface GeomFillSurface, Surface Sections and Surface BlendCurve
credit.changes: Words in Simplified Technical English, FreeCAD 1.1 names. Made from the examples of three pages: Surface_GeomFillSurface, Surface_Sections and Surface_BlendCurve (https://wiki.freecad.org/Surface_Sections, https://wiki.freecad.org/Surface_BlendCurve), with their curves. The checks read the type of each surface.

hints: Find the workbench selector in the toolbar.
Open the list of workbenches.
Workbench: Surface.

steps.say: Draw four B-spline curves that meet end to end in a closed loop.
steps.why: Four edges in a loop give the boundary of one surface.
steps.explain: The page gives the curves as Python. Two corners are at x -140 mm, y -100 mm and x 175 mm, y -108 mm. Two corners are at x 200 mm, y 101 mm and x -135 mm, y 107 mm, z 70 mm. Each curve has two or three points between its ends.
hints: Use the B-spline tool of the Draft workbench.
Start each curve on the end of the curve before it.
Four curves; the last one ends on the start of the first.

steps.say: Push **{Surface_GeomFillSurface|Fill boundary curves}**. Select the four curves. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The surface stretches across the four boundary curves.

picture.alt: A green surface that fills a loop of four curved edges.

hints: Select the curves in the view while the panel is open.
Add all four edges to the list in the Tasks panel.
Four boundary edges, fill type Stretched.

steps.say: Draw four section curves at different heights: two half circles and two B-splines above them.
steps.explain: The page's example has four curves. A half circle of radius 50 mm is at z 0 mm. A half circle of radius 30 mm is at z 25 mm. B-splines are at z 50 mm and z 100 mm.
hints: Use the arc and B-spline tools of the Draft workbench.
Put each curve higher than the one before.
Half circles r 50 mm at z = 0 mm and r 30 mm at z = 25 mm. B-splines at z = 50 mm and z = 100 mm.

steps.say: Push **{Surface_Sections|Sections}**. Select the four section curves from the bottom to the top. Push **OK**.
steps.why: The surface goes through each section curve in turn.

picture.alt: A green surface that goes through four section curves, from a wide arch to a small one.

hints: The order of the curves sets the order of the surface.
Add the curves to the list in the Tasks panel.
Four sections, from the bottom curve to the top curve.

steps.say: Draw two B-spline curves whose ends are near each other.
steps.explain: The page's example has two curves. One goes from x -20 mm, y -20 mm up to x -18 mm, y 25 mm. One goes from x 60 mm, y 26 mm down to x 33 mm, y -20 mm.
hints: Use the B-spline tool of the Draft workbench.
Leave a gap between the two curves.
Two curves in the XY plane, with a gap of about 50 mm between their lower ends.

steps.say: Push **{Surface_BlendCurve|Blend curve}**. Select an end of each curve.
steps.why: A blend curve joins two edges smoothly at their ends.

picture.alt: A black blend curve that joins the ends of two white curves smoothly.

hints: Select the two end points that face each other.
Change the size of each end in the Property view.
Start: the lower end of the first curve. End: the lower end of the second curve. Sizes -5 mm.

steps.say: Done: a surface from four boundary curves, a surface through four sections and a blend curve.
